record.paper_title: Open Problems in Hydrodynamical Approach to Relativistic Heavy Ion Collisions
record.context_brief: Model degeneracy in hydrodynamic interpretation of QGP observables
record.original_question: How can hydrodynamical modeling of relativistic heavy-ion collisions be used to extract quantitative properties of quark-gluon plasma and the bulk QCD phase transition when very different model scenarios, including continuous emission, sudden freeze-out, final-state cascade calculations, and simplified blast-wave solutions, can reproduce the same observables after suitable parameter choices?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, there exist several open problems in the interpretation of data in terms of the hydro model. These questions require careful examination to extract quantitative and precise information on the properties of QGP.

Furthermore, one should note that several very different physical scenarios within the hydrodynamical approach (e.g. the use of continuous emission, sudden freeze-out and rQMD final state cascade, or some drastically simplified hydro models such as blast wave solution, etc.) can give rise equally good results in reproducing the observables with suitable choices of parameters.

In order to extract more precise information on the properties of the quark-gluon plasma and the mechanism of phase transition in the bulk QCD matter, we should clarify these points and refine the physical parameters used in these approaches.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the relativistic hydrodynamical description of the hot, dense matter produced in high-energy heavy-ion collisions, in which the evolution of the fireball is modeled by the conservation laws \(\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=0\) (with optional shear and bulk viscous corrections) supplemented by a QCD-motivated equation of state \(p=p(\varepsilon)\) that encodes a transition between a quark-gluon plasma phase and a hadronic phase, together with a prescription for converting fluid cells into observable hadrons. Several inequivalent prescriptions are in common use, including: (i) continuous emission throughout the evolution, (ii) sudden freeze-out on a sharp hypersurface (Cooper–Frye on an isothermal or isochronous surface), (iii) hybrid schemes in which the hydrodynamic stage is matched to a hadronic transport cascade (e.g. an rQMD-type afterburner), and (iv) drastically simplified parametrizations such as blast-wave solutions characterized by a few thermal and flow parameters. Empirically, all of these scenarios, after suitable choices of their free parameters (initial conditions, equation of state, transport coefficients, freeze-out temperature and time, flow profile, etc.), can reproduce the same set of bulk observables (single-particle transverse-momentum spectra, anisotropic flow harmonics \(v_n(p_T)\), Hanbury Brown–Twiss radii, particle ratios) within experimental accuracy.

Problem: Develop a quantitative framework that breaks this degeneracy. Specifically, identify a finite set of observables, or functionals of the hydrodynamic solution, whose values are sensitive to the differences among scenarios (i)–(iv) in a way that allows one to extract, in a model-independent manner, intrinsic properties of the underlying QCD matter — in particular the equation of state \(p(\varepsilon)\) in the transition region, the order/nature of the bulk QCD phase transition, and the transport coefficients (shear viscosity to entropy density ratio \(\eta/s\) and bulk viscosity \(\zeta/s\)) — together with rigorous error estimates that account for parameter ambiguities in the freeze-out/hadronization stage.
artifact.status_search_result: The interpretive degeneracy among hydrodynamic freeze-out/hadronization prescriptions remains an active research problem. Modern hybrid frameworks (e.g., MUSIC+UrQMD, Trajectum, JETSCAPE Bayesian analyses) and global Bayesian inference studies (2019–2024) have made substantial progress in constraining the QGP equation of state and transport coefficients, but the precise extraction of bulk properties continues to depend on the choice of particlization scheme and viscous corrections, and competing scenarios still fit data comparably well. No definitive resolution of the model-degeneracy problem has been established.

status_evidence.title: JETSCAPE Bayesian analysis of QGP properties
status_evidence.snippet: We perform a Bayesian model-to-data comparison... constraints on the temperature dependence of specific shear and bulk viscosities... remaining systematic uncertainties from the choice of particlization model.
status_evidence.claim: Particlization/freeze-out choice remains a major systematic in extracting QGP properties.

status_evidence.title: Trajectum: a flexible heavy-ion code
status_evidence.snippet: Different combinations of hydrodynamic and hadronic-cascade settings can reproduce observables with different inferred transport coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: Model ambiguity in the hydro-to-hadron stage persists.
